_comment: Allowed names for problem distractors (CLAUDE.md: distractors come from named misconceptions). Generators, skill files and the lint reject any name not listed here. Descriptions are parent-facing (parent dashboard). Never rename a name; add a new one.

misconceptions.added_as_ones: Added tens as if they were ones (for example 30 + 20 gave 5).
misconceptions.added_both: Added the two given numbers instead of finding the missing one.
misconceptions.added_factors: Added the two numbers instead of multiplying them (3 and 4 gave 7).
misconceptions.added_instead: Added when the problem asked to subtract.
misconceptions.added_tens_to_ones: Added a tens digit to a ones digit instead of matching places.
misconceptions.carried_twice: Carried a ten more than once, or carried when there was nothing to carry.
misconceptions.changed_ones: Changed the ones digit when asked for ten more or ten less.
misconceptions.compared_ones_first: Compared the ones digits first and ignored the tens.
misconceptions.counted_bars_as_ones: Counted each ten-bar as one instead of ten.
misconceptions.counted_factors_not_pairs: Counted every factor instead of counting the factor pairs.
misconceptions.counted_from_one: Counted the starting number as the first count, so the answer is off by one.
misconceptions.counted_groups: Counted the number of groups instead of the total.
misconceptions.counted_tens_as_ones: Treated each ten as a single one when building or reading a number.
misconceptions.crossed_p_itself: Crossed out the prime itself while crossing out its multiples (a prime is never crossed out).
misconceptions.decade_skip: Jumped one ten too far or too few (the answer is off by exactly ten).
misconceptions.digit_swap: Swapped the digits, writing the tens digit where the ones digit belongs (34 as 43).
misconceptions.digit_value_as_digit: Gave the digit itself instead of its value (the 3 in 34 as 3, not 30).
misconceptions.double_counted: Counted some objects twice, so the answer is too big.
misconceptions.dropped_addend: Left one of the addends out of the sum.
misconceptions.even_means_div_by_4: Thought every even number shares by 4 (the rule needs the last two digits).
misconceptions.factor_not_multiple: Mixed up factors and multiples (gave a factor when a multiple was asked for, or the other way round).
misconceptions.forgot_regroup: Did not trade ten ones for a ten (or a ten for ones) when it was needed.
misconceptions.forgot_untrade: Did not break a ten into ten ones before subtracting.
misconceptions.last_digit_only_for_3: Judged sharing by 3 or 9 from the last digit instead of the digit sum.
misconceptions.left_side_only: Looked only at the left side of the equals sign.
misconceptions.leftover_miscounted: Miscounted the leftover item when making pairs.
misconceptions.missed_last_multiple: Stopped crossing out before the last multiple on the grid.
misconceptions.missed_p_squared: Missed the first new multiple to cross out (p x p, such as 25 for 5).
misconceptions.missing_one_and_n: Left out 1 or the number itself when listing or checking factors.
misconceptions.missing_repeated_factor: Wrote a repeated prime only once (12 as 2 x 3 instead of 2 x 2 x 3).
misconceptions.mixed_up_5_and_10: Thought a number ending in 5 can be shared into tens.
misconceptions.multiple_not_factor: Took a multiple of the number for one of its factors.
misconceptions.multiplied_instead: Multiplied when the problem asked to divide.
misconceptions.no_check_made: Answered yes or no without checking for equal groups with none left over.
misconceptions.odd_means_prime: Thought every odd number is a prime.
misconceptions.off_by_b: Landed one multiple too early or too late (left out the first multiple, started at zero, or went one step past).
misconceptions.off_by_group: Used one group too many or too few when finding a product.
misconceptions.off_by_one: The answer is one more or one less than it should be.
misconceptions.off_by_row: Counted one row too many or too few in an array.
misconceptions.off_by_two: The answer is two more or two less than it should be.
misconceptions.one_is_prime: Thought 1 is a prime. A prime needs exactly two different factors.
misconceptions.only_one_rule_for_6: Checked only one of the two rules for 6 (it must share by 2 and by 3).
misconceptions.picked_smaller: Chose the pile with the opposite size (the smaller pile when asked for more, or the larger when asked for fewer).
misconceptions.product_mismatch: Gave primes whose product is not the number.
misconceptions.reversed_order: Put the numbers in the opposite order (greatest to least instead of least to greatest).
misconceptions.reversed_symbol: Used the symbol that points the wrong way (< for > or > for <).
misconceptions.rows_cols_swapped: Swapped the number of rows and the number of columns when building an array.
misconceptions.rows_cols_swapped_wrong: Swapped rows and columns but also changed a number, so the product is different.
misconceptions.rows_plus_cols: Added the rows and columns instead of multiplying them.
misconceptions.skip_middle_pair: Left out a pair of factors in the middle of the list.
misconceptions.smaller_from_larger: Subtracted the smaller digit from the larger digit in each place, whichever was on top.
misconceptions.square_is_prime: Thought a square number such as 4, 9 or 25 is a prime.
misconceptions.stopped_at_composite: Stopped the factor tree with a piece that can still split (a composite).
misconceptions.subtracted_as_ones: Subtracted tens as if they were ones.
misconceptions.swapped_minuend: Mixed up which number to subtract from when writing a subtraction fact.
misconceptions.thought_equal: Chose = for two numbers that are different.
misconceptions.thought_unequal: Chose < or > for two numbers that are equal.
misconceptions.three_means_nine: Thought a number that shares by 3 must also share by 9.
misconceptions.traded_wrong_count: Traded the wrong number of ones when swapping for a ten (or the other way).
misconceptions.tree_with_composite_leaf: Picked a factor tree that still has a composite piece at the bottom.
misconceptions.two_is_not_prime: Thought 2 is not a prime because it is even.
misconceptions.used_tens_digit: Used the tens digit to decide even or odd instead of the ones digit.
misconceptions.used_the_product: Multiplied the two numbers instead of finding their first shared multiple.
misconceptions.wrong_numbers: Picked a fact with the right sign but different numbers, instead of the same three numbers.
misconceptions.wrong_operation: Used a different operation than the one the fact needs.
misconceptions.wrong_place: Answered for the other digit instead of the digit asked about.
misconceptions.wrong_split: Picked a factor pair that does not have the number asked for.
misconceptions.wrong_step: Counted by the wrong step (for example by 2s when asked for 5s).
misconceptions.included_non_factor: Put in a number that is a factor of only one of the two numbers.
misconceptions.missed_largest: Left out the greatest common factor when listing the common factors.
misconceptions.factors_of_one_number: Listed every factor of one number instead of the factors both numbers share.
misconceptions.picked_smallest_common: Gave the smallest common factor above 1 instead of the greatest.
misconceptions.picked_lcm: Gave the least common multiple when the greatest common factor was asked.
misconceptions.picked_prime_factor_only: Gave one shared prime instead of the product of all the shared primes.
misconceptions.picked_smaller_number: Gave the smaller number, which is not a factor of the larger one.
misconceptions.multiplied_all_primes: Multiplied every prime of both prime factorizations (the product of the two numbers).
misconceptions.took_union: Took every prime from either factorization (the least common multiple) instead of the shared ones.
misconceptions.shared_even_only: Thought only even numbers can share a factor, so called two odd numbers coprime.
misconceptions.missed_common_factor: Called two numbers coprime although they share a factor above 1.
misconceptions.assumed_primes_only: Thought only primes can be coprime, so said a coprime pair with a composite shares a factor.
misconceptions.assumed_common_factor: Said two different primes share a factor above 1.
misconceptions.listed_product_only: Listed multiples of the product of the two numbers instead of their least common multiple.
misconceptions.off_by_one_multiple: Started the list of common multiples one step late (skipped the first one).
misconceptions.multiples_of_one_number: Listed multiples of only one of the two numbers.
misconceptions.picked_product: Multiplied the two numbers instead of finding their least common multiple.
misconceptions.picked_gcf: Gave the greatest common factor when the least common multiple was asked.
misconceptions.picked_sum: Added the two numbers instead of finding a common multiple.
misconceptions.took_intersection: Took only the shared primes (the greatest common factor) instead of every prime needed.
misconceptions.dropped_highest_power: Used each prime only once instead of as many times as it shows up in either number.
misconceptions.added_instead_of_multiplied: Thought GCF + LCM equals the sum of the two numbers instead of GCF × LCM equalling their product.
misconceptions.inverted_ratio: Turned the comparison around (multiplied when dividing, or wrote the ratio back to front).
misconceptions.subtracted_teeth: Took the difference of the numbers instead of dividing the teeth.
misconceptions.same_size_gear: Picked a gear the same size as the first, which turns only once.
misconceptions.used_gcf: Used the greatest common factor of the teeth instead of the least common multiple.
misconceptions.counted_other_gear: Counted the turns of the other gear instead of the gear asked about.
misconceptions.teeth_not_turns: Gave the number of teeth that pass (the least common multiple) instead of the turns.
misconceptions.divided_numerator_only: Divided only the top number by the common factor and left the bottom number as it was.
misconceptions.partially_simplified: Divided by a common factor that is not the greatest, so it is not yet in simplest form.
misconceptions.swapped_num_den: Wrote the simplest form upside down (top and bottom swapped).
misconceptions.divided_one_term_only: Divided only the first number of the ratio by the common factor.
misconceptions.inverted: Wrote a fraction upside down: the count of all the shards on top.
misconceptions.counted_shaded_as_denominator: Put the count of the other shards on the bottom (1/3 for one shard of four).
misconceptions.unshaded_count: Counted the dark shards instead of the lit ones.
misconceptions.off_by_one_numerator: Miscounted the lit shards by one.
misconceptions.counted_ticks_not_gaps: Counted the tick marks on a number line instead of the spaces between them.
misconceptions.added_to_both: Made an equivalent fraction by adding the same number to the top and bottom instead of multiplying.
misconceptions.scaled_numerator_only: Multiplied the top of a fraction but kept the bottom.
misconceptions.copied_numerator: Kept the top number (or lit as many shards) as in the first fraction.
misconceptions.compared_denominators: Saw the same bottom numbers and said the fractions are equal.
misconceptions.bigger_denominator_bigger: Thought a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction.
misconceptions.compared_numerators_only: Compared only the top numbers of two fractions.
misconceptions.added_denominators: Added the bottom numbers as well as the tops (1/4 + 2/4 = 3/8).
misconceptions.added_numerators_only: Added the tops and kept a bottom without making the shards the same size.
misconceptions.dropped_whole: Left out the whole crystals of a mixed number.
misconceptions.added_whole_to_numerator: Added the number of wholes to the top instead of their shards.
misconceptions.swapped_quotient_remainder: Swapped the wholes and the leftover shards of a mixed number.
misconceptions.place_shift: Put the decimal point (or a percent's digits) one place off.
misconceptions.read_as_whole: Read the digits of a decimal as a whole number.
misconceptions.dropped_zero: Left out the zero in the tenths place (0.05 written as 0.5).
misconceptions.wrote_numerator_as_decimal: Wrote the top of a fraction after the decimal point.
misconceptions.longer_is_bigger: Thought the decimal with more digits is the bigger one.
misconceptions.ignored_whole: Compared only the digits after the point and ignored the whole numbers.
misconceptions.counted_unlit: Counted the dark cells of the grid instead of the lit ones.
misconceptions.wrote_numerator_as_percent: Wrote the top of a fraction as the percent.
misconceptions.part_to_whole: Compared one part with all the ore instead of with the other part.
misconceptions.added_instead_of_scaled: Scaled a ratio by adding the same amount to both parts instead of multiplying.
misconceptions.scaled_one_part: Grew one part of a ratio but kept the other part the same.
misconceptions.dropped_sign: Left off (or added) the minus sign of a number below zero.
misconceptions.bigger_magnitude_bigger: Thought the number farther from zero is greater, even below zero.
misconceptions.wrong_direction: Moved up the gauge instead of down, or down instead of up.
misconceptions.multiplied_base_by_exp: Multiplied the base by the exponent (3 to the power 4 as 3 × 4).
misconceptions.added_base_exp_times: Added the base again and again instead of multiplying (3 + 3 + 3 + 3 for 3 to the power 4).
misconceptions.swapped_base_exp: Swapped the base and the exponent (4 to the power 3 for 3 to the power 4).
misconceptions.off_by_one_exponent: Multiplied one time too many or too few (one power, one place of ten, or one term of a sequence, off).
misconceptions.doubled: Doubled the number instead of multiplying it by itself (2 × 7 for 7 squared).
misconceptions.off_by_one_square: Squared the number next to it (6 × 6 or 8 × 8 for 7 squared).
misconceptions.tripled: Tripled the number instead of cubing it (3 × 4 for 4 cubed).
misconceptions.squared_only: Multiplied only twice: squared instead of cubed.
misconceptions.halved: Halved the number instead of finding its square root.
misconceptions.off_by_one_root: Gave a square root one too big or one too small.
misconceptions.added_two: Added 2 each time instead of doubling (1, 2, 4, 6, 8).
misconceptions.counted_digits_not_zeros: Wrote as many digits as the exponent instead of as many zeros.
misconceptions.zero_power_is_zero: Thought a number to the power 0 is 0 (it is 1).
misconceptions.first_power_is_one: Thought a number to the power 1 is 1 (it is the number itself).
misconceptions.added_base_and_exp: Added the base and the exponent.
misconceptions.read_as_decimal_digits: Read the digits as an ordinary base-ten number.
misconceptions.reversed_bits: Read or wrote the digits in the wrong order (the ones place is on the right).
misconceptions.dropped_leading_place: Left out the biggest place (the first lamp or digit).
misconceptions.greedy_skipped_place: Left out the 0 for a place that is skipped, so the other digits slid over.
misconceptions.forgot_carry: Added binary columns without carrying (1 + 1 written as 0).
misconceptions.carried_as_decimal: Wrote 2 in a binary column instead of carrying (a base-ten habit).
misconceptions.used_base_two: Used binary places (1, 2, 4) in another base.
misconceptions.counted_digits_not_shift: Wrote the exponent's number of zeros after all the digits instead of moving the point.
misconceptions.mantissa_not_normalized: Left the first number at 10 or more (34 × 10 to the 4 instead of 3.4 × 10 to the 5).
misconceptions.matched_weight_only: Put the same weight on each side without thinking about the distance.
misconceptions.added_distance: Added weight and distance instead of multiplying them.
misconceptions.swapped_distances: Mixed up the two distances (the farther weight pushes harder).
misconceptions.added_wrong_step: Added a step one bigger or smaller than the sequence's own step.
misconceptions.repeated_last_term: Wrote the last number of the sequence again instead of the next one.
misconceptions.averaged_neighbors_wrong: Added the two numbers beside the gap but did not halve the total.
misconceptions.confused_start_and_step: Gave the first number of the sequence as the amount added each time.
misconceptions.added_ratio: Added the ratio to the last number instead of multiplying by it.
misconceptions.continued_by_adding: Kept adding the last difference although the sequence multiplies.
misconceptions.swapped_types: Called an adding sequence a multiplying one, or the other way round.
misconceptions.missed_the_pattern: Said the sequence has no rule although it adds or multiplies the same number.
misconceptions.used_square: Gave the square number (n times n) for a triangular number.
misconceptions.off_by_one_n: Used one row (or one number) too few or too many.
misconceptions.used_triangular: Gave the triangular number for a square number.
misconceptions.added_same_triangular_twice_wrong_n: Doubled one staircase instead of fitting a staircase one row shorter beside it.
misconceptions.added_wrong_pair: Added two numbers that are not the two just before (skipped one).
misconceptions.doubled_last: Doubled the last number instead of adding the two before.
misconceptions.rounded_down: Cut off the digits after the hundredths instead of rounding to the nearest.
misconceptions.forgot_halve: Made the pairs but did not halve: counted every pair twice.
misconceptions.used_n_squared: Multiplied the last number by itself instead of using the pairs.
misconceptions.wrong_diagram: Picked a fact the picture does not show.
misconceptions.wrong_line_count: Picked a line with the syllable count of another line of the poem.
misconceptions.off_by_one_syllable: Counted one syllable too many or too few.
